#897. Efficient catalyst-controlled C–H arylation of arenes

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

We’re sharing this article early to provide faster access to peer-reviewed, accepted research. It is citable and carries a permanent DOI. This version is subject to further edits and will be replaced automatically by the final Version of Record. All legal disclaimers apply.

Direct arylation of C–H bonds in arenes offers a streamlined alternative to widely used cross-coupling reactions.1 However, native substrates lack the preinstalled functional handles that ordinarily provide both reactivity and control over the site of reaction. Consequently, despite long-standing interest in directly engaging C–H bonds as reactive sites,2–4 the design of general catalysts that deliver high yields across diverse substrate classes while controlling site selectivity remains a challenge.5–12 Here we show that a microenvironment around a prototypical palladium dicarboxylate catalytic site can provide high selectivity for direct arylation of sterically exposed C–H sites, while high efficiency is achieved using an advanced palladium(II) precatalyst and tailored diaryliodonium reagents for selective aryl transfer. The applicability of this system spans from electron-rich to electron-deficient arenes, while electron-neutral benzene, which is often a challenge for C–H arylation, undergoes successive sterically controlled arylations, delivering functionalized polyaryl compounds. In addition to removing the necessity for pre-functionalized substrates, the mild conditions enable direct late-stage C–H arylation and the installation of aryl groups equipped with functionalities that are typically either reactive in traditional cross-coupling catalysis, such as triflates, iodides, and boronate esters, or sensitive to the basic conditions, such as N-hydroxysuccinimide esters. The results emphasize the distinct synthetic value of palladium-catalyzed direct C–H arylation reactions and showcase a catalyst platform that facilitates high yields and control over site-selectivity.

Khloe Kardashian said during the Nov. 12 episode of The Kardashians that Lamar Odom has burned his final bridge with her after his comments in his Untold documentary.

Some things, you just don’t come back from.

And for Khloe Kardashian, her ex-husband Lamar Odom’s characterization of their relationship in his Untold Netflix documentary was a bridge too far.

The topic is brought up in the Nov. 12 epsiode of The Kardashians by Scott Disick, who asked, “Hey, did you hear what Lamar said about this new documentary?”

The question prompted Kardashian’s BFF Malika Haqq to note, “I wanted to get his ass.”

ICYMI, in Untold: The Death & Life of Lamar Odom, Odom alleges he only married Kardashian to further his own fame and downplays his ex-wife’s role in ensuring his health and safety in the wake of his near-fatal overdose in 2015—claims that struck deep for Kardashian.

“I don’t need you to thank me, just don’t talk about me,” she said during a confessional during the Kardashians episode. “Don’t discredit me.”

As Kardashian—mom to kids True, 8, and Tatum, 4, with ex Tristan Thompson—put it, “The bridge is burned and there’s no more rope to throw over, so he is dead to me.”

More than anything, the fact Kardashian willingly participated in the documentary, only to have her ex make disparaging comments was the bitter-tasting icing on the cake.

“I’m watching the documentary and I’m like, ‘Wait, I took time out of my life to sit here and do a favor for you,’” the True American founder said in the confessional. “I’m not being paid. I’m doing this ‘cause I’m trying to be nice. And there’s so many things that I just found really distasteful.”

Among them, “saying that you weren’t really in love with me,” Kardashian explained. “You married me just so you could be more popular in pop culture, all these things, which is so weird. Even if that is your truth, why don’t you say it without me being on the other side of these interviews? Like, I just thought that was really, really lame.”

For his part, Odom—dad to three with ex Liza Morales—has since pointed out it was one of his children who specifically alleged he only married Kardashian for the fame, though in Untold he admits to wanting to marry her after seeing the reality star’s family “lifestyle.”

Nevertheless, Kardashian said she has no more patience for such energy.

“This just solidifies what liars, con artists, cheats, thieves, trolls that men are,” she said. “And I just don’t want to be involved. Play with yourself, don’t play with me.”

#895. Danny Kelly, football broadcaster and renowned editor, dies aged 69

Danny Baker pays tribute to the ‘funniest man I knew’

Kelly was former editor of the NME and Q magazines

The journalist and broadcaster Danny Kelly, who helped define coverage of music and football in the UK for a generation, has died at the age of 69.

Kelly edited the NME and Q magazine, and launched the Football 365 website before going on to be a presenter and pundit on the BBC and TalkSport. He had been receiving treatment for oesophageal cancer.

Tributes were led by Kelly’s longstanding broadcast partner Danny Baker. “My great friend, supreme broadcaster and funniest man I ever knew, Danny Kelly, died yesterday afternoon,” Baker wrote on social media, the pair having worked together on any number of radio, TV shows and podcasts. “I cannot believe I will never hear his voice again.”

Tottenham Hotspur paid emotional tribute to Kelly, a lifelong Spurs fan. A statement said: “The entire Tottenham family mourns the loss of one of our own, broadcasting legend Danny Kelly. Our thoughts and love are with his family and friends at this incredibly sad time.”

TalkSport, for which Kelly worked as a presenter for nearly two decades, said it was “heartbroken” by the news. “A cherished part of TalkSport for so many years, Danny brought extraordinary wit, warmth and knowledge to our airwaves,” the station said. “His passion for football, music and life was infectious, and his kindness touched everyone around him.”

Another broadcaster, the former Sky Sports host Richard Keys, said Kelly “was all of the things – and more – being said about him – ‘warm, witty and knowledgable’”.

Kelly was born in north London in 1956 and first made his name writing about music. He began contributing to the NME in his 20s and went on to edit the agenda-setting weekly newspaper at the end of the 1980s. From there he took charge of the top-selling music monthly Q magazine, where he was named British magazine editor of the year.

Manic Street Preachers paid tribute to “a brilliant broadcaster-writer-ideas factory. Danny was editor of the NME when we first started getting press, a wonderful man, his musical knowledge was vast and deep, his radio voice has been part of our lives for so long … We will all miss him.”

In the second half of the 1990s, Kelly threw himself into the nascent world of digital media and launched Football365, which became one of the leading online voices on the sport. In the noughties, he spotted another development – podcasts – and launched the Game, a weekly football podcast, for the Times.

Over the past 15 years Kelly became best known as a radio presenter and podcast host, including presenting the Tottenham-focused show View from The Lane. Paying tribute to “our host, our leader” on its X account, the View from the Lane said: “We all loved him as much as he loved Spurs.”

#893. Anthony Clark, Yes, Dear Star and Comedian, Dead at 62

Anthony Clark, a comedian known for his roles in Yes, Dear and Boston Common, has died, his former castmate Mike O’Malley confirmed. He was 62.

Anthony Clark, a comedian who starred in Yes, Dear and Boston Common, died Nov. 10, his former castmate Mike O’Malley confirmed in a post on social media. He was 62.

“He was a hilarious guy,” O’Malley wrote in a tribute shared to Instagram Nov. 12. “He was so unique—one of those comics who is laughing along with you at the absurdity of his stories and observations and it just made you laugh harder because he was laughing. I was a fan before I was a friend. We spoke on the phone three weeks ago. He had us laughing loudly as he always did.”

O’Malley—who starred alongside Clark on Yes, Dear—included photos from their last day of set, nodding to the sentimental value.

“Attached are some snapshots from our last episode of ‘Yes Dear’ which ended twenty years ago,” he continued. “He invested his money well and essentially retired after we wrapped. Rest in peace, Tony.”

Hailing from Virginia and attending Emerson College, Clark made his television debut on American Playhouse in 1991. He went on to score roles in Ellen DeGeneres’ sitcom Ellen and the romantic comedy The Thing Called Love before booking the role of Boyd Pritchett on Boston Common in 1996.

From there, he secured his role as studio executive Greg Warner in Yes, Dear for 122 episodes alongside O’Malley, as well as Jean Louisa Kelly and Liza Snyder. Having also established a career in stand-up in tandem with his acting, Clark hosted the fourth season of The Last Comic Standing in 2006.

Following his performance in Yes, Dear, Clark made a few additional minor appearances in films before retreating from the spotlight entirely.

Still, those who did get to know him would agree with how his agent Barry Katz put it in his own tribute, noting that Clark was “arguably one of the funniest people that I have ever met in my lifetime.”

#891. Complaint filed to IRS in relation to Fifa head Gianni Infantino’s housekeeper

It calls for inquiry into claims she was on Fifa payroll

Fifa: Infantino personally pays for ‘any domestic staff’

A complaint has been filed to the United States Internal Revenue Service calling for an investigation into claims an individual on the Fifa payroll was working privately as a housekeeper for Gianni Infantino.

If the IRS investigates and finds the claims to be proven then Fifa could lose its tax-exempt status in the US. Fifa has 501(c)(4) status in the country, a category for organisations “created to promote community welfare for charitable, educational or recreational purposes”.

The complaint, which has been seen by the Guardian and is supported by a number of documents, claims an individual “performed domestic work exclusively for Fifa president Gianni Infantino and his wife, Leena Infantino, at their Miami residence, while receiving compensation or benefits through a Fifa-affiliated entity”, and argues that “senior leadership, acting in their official capacity and on behalf of Fifa, have abused the entity’s tax-exemption status”.

In the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.

If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.

If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from the iOS App Store on iPhone or the Google Play store on Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.

The complaint goes on to argue: “If organisational funds or resources were used to pay for services benefiting a leader’s household, the arrangement raises serious questions about private benefit, financial reporting, compensation, and governance. The materials also raise questions about the accuracy of representations in employment, payroll, tax, and immigration records. We ask the agencies to investigate the underlying records and determine what occurred.” The IRS has been approached for comment.

The news comes as Fifa’s activities, and specifically Infantino’s involvement in the failed Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme and his relationship with the Trump White House, are to come under intensified scrutiny from Democratic politicians in the US after the “blue wave” at the midterm elections. A spokesperson for the ranking member of the House judiciary committee, representative Jamie Raskin, said the committee had not requested documents related to the housekeeper but was “looking closely at those developments”.

A Fifa spokesperson said: “Matters related to the Fifa president’s personal and home life are private; however, for the avoidance of any doubt, the costs of any domestic staff are met by the Fifa president personally.”

The complaint, if taken up, would probably take months to complete and commonly the results of IRS investigations are not published. Any action taken as a result, however, would be in the public domain. The complaint was submitted by the Washington DC lawyer Abed Ayoub, who works in immigration law and has served as the national executive director of the American-Arab Anti-Discrimination Committee (ADC). Last year the ADC was part of the campaign Game Over Israel, which called for Israeli football teams to be banned from international competition.

Fifa said: “We urge the media to act responsibly. As Fifa stated in August, it is evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine Fifa and its president. Fifa welcomes legitimate scrutiny. But scrutiny is not a licence to amplify false allegations. Where reporting is inaccurate or misleading Fifa will continue to challenge it directly and vigorously.”

Infantino has been described by his predecessor, Sepp Blatter, as a “dictator” who “no longer knows any borders”. Blatter, Fifa’s president for 17 years before resigning amid a corruption scandal at the organisation, made the remarks in an interview with the German magazine Der Spiegel. He criticised the FFE scheme, the Fifa peace prize and, most significantly in his opinion, the overturning of Folarin Balogun’s suspension for a red card during the World Cup.

Our picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown in

“Fifa is suffering,” Blatter said. “It is currently led by a person who has allowed himself to be blinded.” He described the peace prize as “embarrassing”, saying: “Why would he do something like that? Infantino awards a peace prize to someone who wages war against Iran shortly afterwards?”

In assessing the FFE scheme, which was abandoned after an international outcry, Blatter said: “Infantino no longer knows any borders. He doesn’t understand any of this.” He described the Balogun controversy as “the worst”, saying: “Statutes can be interpreted. But rules of the game must apply to everyone, you can’t interpret them.”

#890. Bachelor's Peter Weber Announces Engagement to Jadeyn Carr

The Bachelor alum Peter Weber confirmed that he and Jadeyn Carr, with whom he’s expecting twins, are engaged.

Peter Weber has given away his final rose.

Two months after the Bachelor alum shared that he is expecting twins with Jadeyn Carr—whom he hard-launched in September—he announced that they are engaged.

Alongside a snap of the model showing off her oval-cut diamond ring in a Nov. 11 Instagram post, Weber wrote, "Marry Me @jaydencarr."

Meanwhile, Carr reacted to the news on her Instagram Stories, adding, "my forever!!!"

And it was a Bachelor Nation reunion in the comments of the announcement. In fact, fellow Bachelor alum Adam Gottschalk revealed that wife Raven Gottschalk—whom he met on season four of Bachelor in Paradise—had an inkling that wedding bells were in the near distance.

"Dang it, I lost a bet with Raven that you were gonna propose on a plane," he admitted with two laughing emojis. "Congrats bro! You guys are gonna be amazing parents."

Bachelor Nation star Tyler Cameron also congratulated him, writing, "Nicely done sir!!"

Life has been coming up roses for Weber, with the couple announcing Carr's pregnancy in September. The 35-year-old (also known as Pilot Pete) captioned a photo booth strip, in which he was kissing his love's growing bump, "1 + 1 = 4."

But the commercial airline pilot's love life wasn't always a fairy tale. He initially got down on one knee for Hannah Ann Sluss in 2020's season 24, though they broke off their engagement before the finale. He also briefly dated runner-up Madison Prewett, with whom he split from two days after the final episode aired.

He eventually found love with former contestant Kelley Flanagan for seven months, until December 2020, before picking up their romance again from August 2022 to April 2023. Though Weber's past relationships didn't work out, the reality star didn't lose hope about finding his person.

"You can't ever force it, but I have faith in due time that'll work out," he told People in February 2025. "I never lost faith, so I know it'll happen soon, and I'm just enjoying the journey along the way."

As for what kind of woman Weber was looking for? He added, "Just someone that I can truly just be myself with and fully let go and relax with and have that sense of peace with."

As Weber and Carr embrace their latest relationship milestone, keep reading to see where more Bachelor Nation couples stand.

Even before Mel Owen's season of The Golden Bachelor kicked off, he was hit with a few penalties after going on the MGoBlue Podcasts With Jon Jansen and insisting, "if they’re 60 or over, I’m cutting them," adding that he wanted them to "try to stay away from the artificial hips and the wigs."

And while Peg Munson is a fellow sexagenarian, his connection with the retired firefighter and bomb tech was quite explosive, with the former NFL linebacker praising her as "high-energy" to Glamour.

Though he didn't take a knee during his November 2025 finale, the sports lawyer still offered up a Neil Lane sparkler, saying, "This represents our commitment to love, to give us time to figure out together what our future holds."

Munson announced in October 2026 that the couple had split, sharing on Instagram, "I did have to make the difficult decision to step away from the relationship. Sometimes, even when there's love, it just doesn't turn out the way that we hoped. So right now, I'm just, I'm just focusing on healing my heart and just focusing on myself, my health, and looking forward to the next chapter.”

According to Spencer Conley (who intrigued Jenn Tran with his "golden retriever energy" on The Bachelorette), he fetched quite the catch on the 10th season of Bachelor in Paradise. Posting a snippet of himself and Jess Edwards (she took a swing at Bachelor Joey Graziadei's heart) revealing that they were falling for one another—Bachelor code for I'm not quite ready to say, "I love you"—he wrote on his Instagram Stories in August 2025 that he'd "already won."

Hard same from Jess, who wrote on her main feed, "just feeling a lil giddy about this man & whatnot."

And they were certainly smiling when, after choosing their relationship over the $250,000 prize, they got engaged and walked away with a surprise check worth $190,000.

"Everything that we’ve been through," Jess said, "has led us to this exact moment."

Since then, their love led her to Dallas, Jess revealing during Mel's November 2025 After the Finale Rose special that she was Texas-bound in a few weeks.

"This was my best first date," Bailey Taylor Brown wrote on Instagram in August 2025 after she took Jeremy Simon out on Paradise's 10th season. And perhaps her last? The social media manger, who initially competed for Grant Ellis' heart, and the real estate investor who nearly charmed Bachelorette Jenn managed to survive their most dramatic squabble ever when she learned he had second thoughts about sending Susie Evans home.

Still, their connection continued to heat up in Costa Rica. And while they were sent home during the Bachelor in Paradise finale, they continued to pursue a relationship off-camera. In fact, the show revealed that they've met each other families and that they're planning to move to the same city.

"We feel so lucky to have found each other," Bailey wrote on Instagram in September 2025, "and couldn’t be more excited for what’s to come."

Seems the connection between Paradise season 10 pair Andrew Spencer (one of Katie Thurston's suitors) and Alexe Godin (from Grant's season) has remained trés strong post-show. Six days after the Chicago-based football player dubbed the pedatric speech therapist "mon amour" in an August 2025 Instagram post, she labeled him "mon chéri" in her own missive.

And while they chose love over the $250,000 prize during the BiP finale, they still got to head home with $125,000 in their pockets.

"This is frickin unreal," Alexe said. "I am leaving with money, but not just money—love, the most important thing."

And they're bringing their love to the Windy City, with the show revealing Alexe's plans to move to Chicago with Andrew.

"Finally found someone just as weird as me," she wrote on Instagram in September 2025, "and I can’t wait to do life with you."

Kat Izzo and Dale Moss went through a thorny moment during the Bachelor in Paradise finale when former contestant Sean McLaughlin alleged she "stashed a laptop" and had been sending an ex love letters. However, the nurse practitioner denied contacting him on the show.

"Did me and my ex still have a relationship prior to this?" she said. "Yes, because I didn’t think I was gonna meet anybody here."

While Kat and Dale were sent home before the final test of Paradise, their romance continued to bloom. The show revealed the alum from Zach Shallcross' season and the former contestant from Clare Crawley's went on to travel across the U.S. together and made plans to build a future together, including moving closer.

"It was tough at times," Dale commented under Kat's August 2025 Instagram post, "but we navigated it together…and I wouldn’t change a thing."

But their journey came to a close in early 2026.

Among the issues Kat detailed during a January appearance on the Bachelor Happy Hour podcast was his unwillingness to relocate from NYC.

"San Diego is apparently, to him, not anywhere he could grow his career," she explained. "I never really got full answers. I don’t really know what the true reason was."

Golden Bachelorette alum Gary Levingston and Leslie Fhima (a runner up for Golden Bachelor Gerry Turner's heart) appeared to have quite the glittery future when they were voted off Bachelor in Paradise's 10th season, even writing about "making new memories" in a post-elimination social media video. But the onetime Prince muse isn't quite sure if she wants to be his lover.

"We talk all the time," she revealed during an August 2025 appearance on Bachelor Happy Hour. "Gary is, I can honestly say right now, one of my best friends. I’ll call him if I have a problem. He kind of talks me off the ledge a little bit, and we are always there for each other. We have each other’s back."

While she acknowledged that the nearly 2,000 miles between them (she's based in Minnesota; he's in California) complicates the situation, she hasn't given up hope. "All I know is that for me, a big thing with any relationship, a romantic one for sure, is I want to be friends first," she continued. "Because I want to be with my best friend growing older."

Golden Bachelorette's head mansion man Kim Buike found someone to make sweet music with in Gerry Turner's first impression rose recipient Faith Martin. Though they were eliminated on the 10th season of Paradise, they sailed off into the sunset, with Faith posting a video to Instagram in August 2025 of the retired navy captain enjoying a hometown date with her in Washington.

However, they ultimately realized they weren't each other's person and that they were better off as friends.

"We talk sometimes two to three times a week," Faith said in a September 2025 Instagram video. "He lives five and a half hours away. But the point is this: We are not a in-love couple. Nope, we are not. We never fell in love. We had a great connection on the show."

#889. Pochettino expected to lead US in Nations League games before Manchester United move

USMNT coach agreed framework of a deal with United

United have made contact with US federation

Balogun: ‘I’d like to keep things the way they are’

Live news and reaction for Pochettino’s move to Man Utd

Mauricio Pochettino will lead the US men’s national team through the remainder of this international window, a source with direct knowledge of US Soccer’s plans told the Guardian on Thursday.

Pochettino has emerged as the leading candidate to replace Michael Carrick, who was sacked as Manchester United manager on Thursday. The Guardian previously reported that the framework of a deal had been agreed between Pochettino and United. The Athletic was first to report news of Pochettino’s plans for the upcoming US matches.

The USMNT face Haiti on Saturday and then again on Tuesday in Miami and Cincinnati, respectively, in the quarter-finals of the Concacaf Nations League. Pochettino has been leading the US through training at the federation’s headquarters and training facility outside Atlanta this week. The Argentinian has yet to publicly address his link to United, though he is scheduled to speak to reporters on Friday morning.

United have also officially made contact with US Soccer in an approach for Pochettino’s services, multiple sources familiar with the negotiations said Thursday. Pochettino and his representatives had already ironed out details of a proposed agreement, with the Argentinian keeping the federation appraised of those ongoing talks. United would need to pay a buyout clause of $10m (£7.5m) to hire Pochettino and millions more, reportedly, to bring along his longtime assistant coaching staff, who are also expected to make the move.

At US training this week, Pochettino’s players have addressed the still-fluid situation surrounding their head coach. Striker Folarin Balogun told reporters on Thursday that “If I had a vote, I’d like to keep things the way they are.”

On Tuesday, defender Antonee Robinson downplayed the significance of Pochettino’s reported departure.

Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer.

“As a soccer player, we’re pretty used to sort of fast training environments and games … so we’re all very good at just focusing on the next task and about the next session or the next game coming up,” Robinson said. “For me personally, I don’t really look at it … It’s just focusing on we’ve got a game at the weekend and I’m going to do everything I can to be ready to play for him, and how he wants us to play.”

#884. Lionel Richie Breaks Silence Nearly 2 Months After Heart Procedure

Lionel Richie was happy to report he’s back during his Nov. 11 residency concert at The Wynn in Las Vegas, occurring two months after he underwent a heart procedure.

It’s Lionel Richie fans have been looking for, and he’s back to say hello.

The 77-year-old took a moment of his Nov. 11 residency performance at The Wynn in Las Vegas to address his recent health scare—during which time he underwent a heart procedure—assuring fans he was ready to boogie all night long.

“I’m back,” an increasingly emphatic Richie told the crowd three times during the show, before quipping, “I don’t know where I was, but I’m back.”

“I’m doing just fine,” he emphasized, as seen in a video shared by @jpasc24 on Instagram. “Thank you all so much for caring about me.”

And with the arms of the crowd open wide in welcome, Richie decided to turn the evening into one of celebration—with one specific honoree in mind.

“I want to make it a tribute tonight, to me,” he exclaimed. “I better make a tribute to myself before somebody else has that show down the street, ‘Come see Lionel Richie down the street!’”

But why stop at just one night? As Richie noted, “Wait a minute, no, this is gonna be a whole week of celebrating Lionel Richie.”

However, after some dancing on the ceiling—or, in this case, some jumping around the stage—a winded Richie took a moment to refuel.

“That was too much, that was beyond my electrolyte capabilities,” he said, after which a crew member brought Richie a glass of red electrolytes. “Now let me tell y’all something, for years I thought that water was important. And then, one day, I got dizzy and I said bring me some water, and the man said, ‘You don’t need water, you need electrolytes.’”

“All these years, drinking water,” Richie joked. “So now I drink electrolytes for breakfast, lunch and dinner, and then the doctor told me you need to eat some food. And I said, ‘Well, the last food I ate, the chickens, was contaminated, then the lettuce became contaminated, so what the hell are you supposed to eat?’”

But thankfully, the electrolytes seemed to do the trick.

“Now that I feel refreshed,” a reenergized Richie said, walking towards his piano, “I’m gonna play a song.”

Richie’s onstage celebration comes just under two months since he underwent a routine heart procedure to treat Atrial fibrillation, commonly known as Afib.

At the time, his rep shared in a Sept. 22 statement, “The doctor said everything went perfectly. Lionel is doing great but will take some time off and will be back on stage soon.”

But while Richie is fully on the mend, he’s not the only celebrity to have had to navigate a challenging health scare. Read on for more.

The Jessie alum opened up about her "hellish" migraines, sharing how they've worsened after suffering five concussions over the course of her life.

"The brain injuries make things significantly worse," Ryan shared during a September 2026 episode of Mythical Kitchen’s Last Meals. "I had a pretty crazy, life-altering brain injury a few years ago, and I was out of commission for six months."

While Ryan described her first four concussions as "incidents," she said her fifth one was trauma caused by "sustained shaking over a minute of time."

Now, the former Disney Channel star needs to close her eyes to "think better."

"Quite often the world is really loud. It’s really too bright. There’s a lot going on," she explained. "The visual data that I'm taking in can be so distracting and so loud. Then, with the migraines—which are significantly worsened by that—it sort of is too much."

Brianna "Chickenfry" LaPaglia's Ovarian Cyst

In May 2026, the BFFs podcaster underwent emergency surgery after doctors discovered a large ovarian cyst that had been twisting her organs and causing internal bleeding.

"There was a half a liter of blood in my pelvic floor," Brianna shared in a TikTok video after the operation. "I have five incisions all over my stomach. They went in through my belly button with a camera so they could find all the blood."

The Total Bellas alum revealed that one of her breast implants shifted after an elbow slam from fellow WWE star Piper Niven during a July 2025 wrestling match.

"It's OK," she told sister Bella Garcia at the time. "We're going to get it fixed one day. I told the doctor, I go, 'Newly divorced, so the minute the boots are hung up, I'm going to come back to you and we're going to make these girls look real good, because these girls are going to get some action in the future and that can't look like that.'"

In October 2026, the former The Bachelorette star detailed how she cracked a vertebra in her spine after setting her vibration plate—a motorized platform that rapidly moves back and forth to promote muscle activation and circulation—to "level 30, supersonic speed."

"Seemingly, subtly, somewhere on the way to 30, maybe 10 or 20, my vertebrae turn crooked and rub against each other," Windey shared in a Substack essaye aptly titled "Broke back, no mountain."

"It was too fast vibrations I guess, and too many vibrations maybe, and too much pressure to shake," she continued. "And it broke. Broke right off, like your ex-boyfriend’s bumper. Well, technically, it cracked."

The injury left her with what she described as "insatiable" paresthesia—a medical term for a tingling, pins-and-needles sensation.

"This is the greatest sense of condemnation; of persecution, I’ll ever feel," she added. "And I do wish it on my worst enemy If only they hadn’t wished it on me first."

The 12 Years a Slave star was diagnosed with uterine fibroids—non-cancerous growths that develop in or around the uterus—in 2014, the same year she won an Oscar for performance in the movie.

However, it wasn't until 2025 when she disclosed her diagnosis, writing on Instagram that she had been "suffering in silence" for more than a decade.

"When we reach puberty, we're taught periods mean pain, and that pain is simply part of being a woman," she shared. "We're struggling alone with something that affects us most."

The Beverly Hills, 90210 alum revealed in April 2025 that he was recovering from surgery after his appendix nearly burst.

“Last week, I started feeling some pain in my stomach,” Brian said in an Instagram video at the time. “I ended up going to the emergency room, and I had a perforated appendix. Not quite burst, but just before.”

He added, “I'm on the road to recovery. It's not an easy process. This is my first major surgery.”

In July 2025, the Daisy Jones & The Six star shared that she had been hospitalized due to a hernia—a gap in the muscular wall that's commonly found in the abdomen or groin area—caused by wearing tight pants.

"'Suki you never tweet anymore,'" she wrote on X, formerly known as Twitter. "Have you ever considered I wore pants so tight 6 months ago it caused a hernia & I’ve been too scared to tell you?"

Savannah DeMelo's Mid-Game "Medical Emergency" Mid-Game

The Racing Louisville midfielder collapsed just a few minutes into her soccer team's September 2025 match against Seattle Reign at Lumen Field in Seatle.

The United States Women’s National Team player could be seen slowly sitting down on the field with a teammate by her side, per Reuters, as the referee called for trainers to check her out. She collapsed seconds later.

“Savannah received immediate on-field care from medical personnel and was transported to a local hospital for further evaluation,” the National Women’s Soccer League wrote on X later that night. “She is stable and alert."

Adam Devine's Long-Term Injury From Childhood Accident

Adam Devine shared that injuries he sustained after getting hit by a cement truck when he was 11 years old are still affecting him to this day.

“It’s been a nightmare,” Devine said in a 2025 episode of the In Depth With Graham Bensinger podcast. “I have spasms all over. For a while, [the doctors] told me I was dying—literally, within this last year.”

He noted that pain comes and goes, adding, "My body has all these things that are a little wonky and a little wrong with it."

The Bachelor Nation alum shared that he went to the hospital “crawling on all fours” due to overwhelming back pain that was aggravated during an RV trip with a friend.

“Right now, knees to my toes, it’s, like, still tingly, which is crazy,” he said on a March 2025 episode of his Trading Secrets podcast. “And to put in perspective, I don’t know, man, like not to sound douchey, but like two, three weeks ago, maybe a month ago, I was squatting probably like 295 pounds. And right now, I can’t do a squat on my foot. I can’t do a one legged squat, I fall. It’s like I had a stroke or something.”

But with the help of a back specialist and some steroids, he added, “We’re on the mend.”

Real Housewives of Orange County’s Gina Kirschenheiter shared her ex-husband Matt Kirschenheiter suffered a heart attack in March 2025, but thankfully survived the ordeal.

The 30 Rock star suffered a health scare at a New York Knicks basketball game in March 2025, leading to him being wheeled out of Madison Square Garden.

However, the comedian shared an update on social media the following day, noting it was a case of food poisoning and that he was on the mend.

The Even Stevens alum shared in February 2025 that she was shot in the face while on a trip to shoot clay pigeons to celebrate husband Brendan Rooney's birthday.

"There was another party with us and they unsafely fired in the wrong direction and shot me in the face," she wrote on Instagram. "@thebrendanrooney immediately sprung into action, assessed me, and rushed me to the hospital. I was hit in 5 places, one was less than an inch from hitting me directly in my right eye."

The Kim Possible alum continued, "Unfortunately a fragment got lodged behind my eye and it is too risky to remove surgically at this time. Doctors will continue to monitor me (I can see normally at the moment)."

The actress said she was grateful to be alive. "I love my daughters, husband, family, and friends so much," she said. "I saw my life flash before my eyes and I’m telling you, hug the people around you every chance you can. Life can change in an instant."

While the internet isn't always a kind place, Amy Schumer is happy that, in this case, it helped her get answers."The internet really came for me after doing a bunch of press, and I was like, 'OK everybody, relax,'" Amy recalled of her "puffier" face on a January 2025 episode of Call Her Daddy. "But then doctors were chiming in in the comments and they were like, 'No no, we think something’s really up. Your face looks so crazy that we think something’s up. And I’m like, ‘Wait, I’m getting trolled by doctors?’"After these doctors said they thought she had Cushing syndrome and that it may be caused by spiking coritsol levels or steroid injections, the Life & Beth creator thought, "Wait, I have been getting steroid injections in my scars.""I had a breast reduction, a C-section, whatever, and so I was getting these steroid injections," Amy said. "So it gave me this thing called Cushing syndrome, which I wouldn’t have known if the internet hadn’t come for me so hard."Toda, Amy is just relieved she's OK. As she shared in a February 2024 News Not Noise newsletter, "Finding out I have the kind of Cushing that will just work itself out and I'm healthy was the greatest news imaginable."

Casey Fitzgerald's Neck Injury From Hockey Skate Blade

The AHL player was cut by a fellow player's skate during a game in December 2024 and received 25 stitches. His father, New Jersey Devils general manager Tom Fitzgerald later told ESPN after his son was fully recovered, "We're very lucky. I don't wish that on any parent."

Hailey Bieber had the "scariest moment" of her life when she was having breakfast with husband Justin Bieber and started experiencing stroke-like symptoms in March 2022."Justin was like, 'Are you OK?'" the Rhode skincare mogul shared a month later on YouTube, "and I just didn't respond because I wasn't sure. And then he asked me again and when I went to respond, I couldn't speak. The right side of my face started drooping. I couldn't get a sentence out."While Hailey said the facial drooping stopped and her speech came back, she went to the hospital to make sure she was OK."They did some scans and they were able to see that I had suffered a small blood clot to my brain," the model added, "which they labeled and categorized as something called a TIA [Transient Ischemic Attack]."Later, Hailey went to the University of California, Los Angeles, where she found out she had a hole in her heart called a patent foramen ovale (PFO).She explained the blood clot had traveled into her heart, "escaped" through the hole and went to her brain, leading to the TIA.Hailey said she had a successful PFO closure procedure and was now feeling great.

The same year Hailey had her health scare, Justin experienced one of his own.In June 2022, the "Baby" singer shared he was diagnosed with Ramsay Hunt syndrome, a condition that caused temporary paralysis to parts of his face and forced him to cancel the remainder of his Justice World Tour."It is from this virus that attacks the nerve in my ear and my facial nerves and has caused my face to have paralysis," Justin explained in an Instagram video at the time. "As you can see, this eye is not blinking. I can't smile on this side of my face. This nostril will not move. So, there's full paralysis on this side of my face."In fact, he told his followers it had gotten "progressively harder to eat." But after a while, the paralysis went away."He's doing really well," Hailey said on a June 2022 episode of Good Morning America, later adding, "He's feeling a lot better. Obviously, it was just a very scary and random situation to happen, but he's going to be totally OK and I'm just grateful that he's fine."

While Jamie Foxx initially kept details of his April 2023 hospitalization private, he later opened up about what he went through.One day in Atlanta, "I was having such a bad headache, so I asked my boy, I said, ‘Listen, I need an aspirin,’” the Oscar winner said in his 2024 Netflix special What Had Happened Was... “Before I could get the Aspirin, I went out. I don’t remember 20 days.”Jamie said he was initially taken to a doctor who gave him a cortisone shot and then sent him home. However, his concerned sister Deidra Dixon then drove him to a hospital, where they got an answer: He had a brain bleed that led to a stroke.Twenty days after undergoing an operation, the Django Unchained woke up May 4 in a wheelchair and couldn’t walk. He then went to Chicago for rehabilitation and therapy."All I can tell you is that I appreciate every prayer,” he said, “because I needed every prayer.”

Tracey Yukich's Medical Emergency on The Biggest Loser

The reality star revealed that she "died" while running a mile during the first challenge of the NBC competition series.

“I don't remember a lot,” she explained on Fit for TV: The Reality of The Biggest Loser. “I remember hearing the helicopter. I just felt like I was floating. And then my grandpa was there. And then I saw darkness. But then I saw light. So I knew, I knew I died that day.”

“My organs were literally shutting down,” she continued. “I didn't realize that I had rhabdomyolysis. And rhabdomyolysis is your body's way of saying, ‘I'm going to shut down on you.’”

Emilia Clarke filmed battle scenes for Game of Thrones, but in 2019, she published an essay in The New Yorker titled "A Battle for My Life."Having a bad headache at the gym, "I reached the toilet, sank to my knees, and proceeded to be violently, voluminously ill," the actress wrote. "Meanwhile, the pain—shooting, stabbing, constricting pain—was getting worse. At some level, I knew what was happening: my brain was damaged."She was taken to the hospital for a brain scan."The diagnosis was quick and ominous: a subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), a life-threatening type of stroke, caused by bleeding into the space surrounding the brain," the Emmy nominee added. "I’d had an aneurysm, an arterial rupture."Emilia had immediate surgery to seal the aneurysm, calling the pain "unbearable." While she was recovering, she continued, she experienced aphasia and was "muttering nonsense."A week later, "the aphasia passed," Emilia added, and she left the hospital a month after being admitted. At a 2013 brain scan, she learned a growth "doubled in size" and that she needed surgery again."When they woke me, I was screaming in pain," she wrote. "The procedure had failed. I had a massive bleed and the doctors made it plain that my chances of surviving were precarious if they didn’t operate again. This time they needed to access my brain in the old-fashioned way—through my skull."Thankfully, Emilia shared, she's now "at a hundred per cent."

Snoop Dogg's daughter Cori Broadus is grateful for her family.Because after she suffered a "severe stroke" in January 2024, her loved ones rushed to be by her side."I texted them that I just had a stroke and sent them a picture," she told E! News correspondent Will Marfuggi in December 2024. "Everybody just came to my rescue."Because of other medical concerns, Cori ended up staying in the hospital longer than she initially expected."I could have went home after my stroke, but my lupus wasn't doing so well," the Snoop's Fatherhood: Cori and Wayne's Story star continued. "My kidneys were failing. It was a lot going on."Today, Cori is on the mend."I'm doing great," she added. "I just had a little bit of motor skills that I had to work back on. But other than that, I was fine."

Shailene Woodley’s early 20s were not an easy time health-wise.“It got to the point where I was losing my hearing. I couldn’t walk for longer than five minutes at a time without having to lay down for hours, and hours and sleep. Everything I ate hurt my stomach,” the actress said on a September 2024 episode of the SHE MD Podcast. “It was this conflation of issues and diagnoses and different doctors telling me different things.”So Shailene—who chose to keep the exact condition private—set out to find answers. “I come from a very holistic background and study herbalism,” she added. “So I was very keen on, ‘I’m going to work with real MDs, [and] I’m also going to work with independent kind of healers.’ Just trying to search for some sense of comfort in my own skin.”It was a long journey—one that lasted for 10 years.“Throughout that decade, a lot of other things came from feeling so much discomfort physically,” the Big Little Lies star noted, “which was, ‘My gosh, if everything I eat hurts my stomach, I’m now suddenly afraid of food.’ And then going into the kind of mental f--ckery that can happen with that of body dysmorphia and confusion about identity and feeling safe in my own capsule, in my own skin, what that meant, and what that should be.”After tending to both her physical and mental health, Shailene is feeling much better.“It was a journey that ultimately physically resolved itself, and I am very healthy,” she shared. “I’m so happy to be able to say that."

#882. DJ Khaled Details Journey to 75-Pound Weight Loss Transformation

After DJ Khaled underwent a 75-pound weight-loss journey the “I’m the One” rapper revealed his health secrets in an exclusive E! News interview as part of his “Walk, Golf…And Wegovy” campaign.

These days, DJ Khaled isn’t going for another one—especially when it comes to food.

After the “I’m the One” rapper sparked major attention for his 75-pound weight loss, he confirmed his transformation happened with the help of the GLP-1 Wegovy, as well as some major lifestyle changes.

“My kids and my wife inspired me,” the 50-year-old told E! News’ Will Marfuggi in an exclusive interview. “When I turned 50, I woke up and thought, ‘You know, it’s time to take it to the next level.’”

And he’s taking fans inside his journey with his “Walk, Golf… And Wegovy” campaign. Along with his medication, Khaled has found that the best music, or rather method, for his weight loss has been through walking—specifically on the golf course. But much like beats, he also switches it up.

“I do gym,” Khaled explained. “I’ve got two treadmills here. I’ve got an elliptical here. I’ve got ropes tied to my tree. I dip and dab into some of the things. When it’s raining, I try to do at least 10,000 steps on the treadmill.”

Starting out, the “All I Do Is Win” hitmaker’s health goal was to simply max out his personal, daily pedometer, but he’s far exceeded his own expectations, noting, “I’ve been getting more than 10,000 steps in a day.”

And while Khaled—dad to Asahd, 10, Aalam, 6, with wife Nicole Tuck—explained that along with his walking routine his doctor “loved the idea” for him to get on Wegovy, he considered that it’s all worked in tandem with his lifestyle changes.

“I stayed consistent with the golf and I noticed I started eating two times a day,” he continued. “I eat lunch around 1 o’clock and then if I want a snack, I’ll eat olives or cucumbers or my kids’ apple sauce—the ones that you squeeze. And then I eat dinner around 8 ‘cause I’m on my kids’ schedule and we eat dinner together when I’m home.”

Reflecting on the last year of his health journey, Khaled called his transformation “beautiful.”

“When you start getting healthier, you just want to do a lot more healthier things because it makes you happier,” he shared. “I think that’s the key. To challenge yourself to do better. Me turning 50, I feel younger than I’ve ever been.”

For more stars who have shared their take on weight loss medications, keep reading…

After years of feeling "very skeptical of starting a GLP-1" actress Chrissy Metz decided it was time to give it a shot. "I'm just very diligent about what and how things work within the body," the This Is Us alum explained in an exclusive August 2026 interview with E! News, "and I'm like, 'Oh, I don't know what that's gonna be like.'"

But after listening to a friend's "very thorough" research, she teamed with telehealth company Ro.

"I've been on diets for a very, very long time, since I was a kid, and I know I can lose weight," she explained, "but I didn't know that I could quiet food noise and I didn't know there were other factors. There's so much shame around being in a bigger body, so just knowing that I wasn't doing it purely for vanity's sake."

Because the result that makes her want to sing its praises is the way it helps her push through eight shows a week in Broadway's & Juliet.

"It's helped with inflammation," she noted. "It's helped with just overall health lab work and blood work and just generally just an overall feeling of space and creativity that the food noise has quieted. It opens up just more ability to be present."

Having gained 80 pounds in back-to-back pregnancies with Malibu Barbie, Elvis and Aquaman, Trisha Paytas was eager to dive into a new weight loss strategy.

"I was starving myself, killing myself in the gym, eating grapefruit for dinner and I just was not losing it," she recounted to People in June 2026. "And I've tried everything else in my life, like all the fad diets, so I was like, 'OK, I should just try a GLP-1 if it's working for so many people.'"

Six weeks into her Zepbound journey, she was down 26 pounds and making plans to run 26.2 miles as she considers a 2027 marathon.

"I've lived 38 years of my life obsessing about food," she explained, "it would be nice to live the next 38 just thinking about food a normal amount."

Following years of struggle following the 2017 birth of eldest daughter Alexis, Serena Williams was ready to serve. "No matter what I did—running, walking, I would walk for hours because they say that’s good," she detailed on Today in 2025, "I literally was playing a professional sport—and I could never go back to where I needed to be for my health."

After a bit of back-and-forth volleying, the Ro partner stuck with a GLP-1 medication that helped her drop 31 pounds.

Sharing her desire to do away with the idea that the medication is a "shortcut," she explained, "As an athlete and as someone that has done everything, I just couldn't get my weight to where I needed to be at a healthy place."

More than three decades after Oprah Winfrey wheeled a wagon of fat onto her talk show stage, she's put her new wellness strategy on display. When she revealed in December 2023 that she was taking a weight loss medication, "I was like an anomaly," she acknowledged on a January 2025 episode of The Oprah Podcast, "an anomaly in that I was willing to say it."

"One of the things that I realized the very first time I took a GLP-1 was that all these years I thought that thin people, those people just had more willpower," she noted. "They ate better foods. They were able to stick to it longer. They never had a potato chip."

But when she started her regimen, she realized "that, 'Oh, they're not even thinking about it. They're only eating when they're hungry and they're stopping when they're full.'"

The couple that pees together also pokes together. Following the 2021 birth of eldest son Riley, singer Meghan Trainor and her actor husband Daryl Sabara did the 75 Hard challenge, "and, man, did we crush,” Meghan detailed during an April 2025 episode of the couple’s Workin’ On It podcast. “Then, we heard more and more of our friends—and even our doctors—were on Mounjaro and Ozempic.”

They each opted to get on the lowest dose possible of Monjaro, combining the shots with exercise and balanced meals. “Daryl and I both do everything together," the "All About That Bass" singer explained. "And we started that journey.”

Years before Dancing With the Stars, the Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star revealed she was taking semaglutide injections—which are sold under brand names like Ozempic and Wegovy—to lose weight.

"I have a secret sauce," she said on YouTube in Janaury 2023. "It's killing the fat and I'm just peeing it out. At least, that's how I understand it."

The Queer Eye star explained in October 2025 that they started using a GLP-1 after a health scare in 2023.

“I decided then that after the medical issue, I was going to get a colonoscopy,” Jonathan said in a TikTok video, “and if I didn't have anything severely wrong with me, I was going to go on a GLP-1, because I just didn't feel good.”

They added, “As I've lost weight and I got into [Pilates classes at] Solidcore, my body has never looked like this,” Jonathan said. “My body's never in my whole life—I've always wanted to have an ab. I've never had abs. And I feel really good, so I'm taking my shirt off a lot.”

Despite losing 70 pounds with the help of the drug, Jonathan re-emphasized their stance on body positivity.

"I'm all about body neutrality,” they continued. “The way that you look does not define your worth, doesn't define your lovableness. You are worth love and worth celebration no matter what your body looks like.”

The comedian has been on the anti-Type 2 diabetes medication Mounjaro since late 2022. In May 2025, she showcased her dramatic weight loss.

"I cant believe this is me now," Rosie wrote on her Instagram, "#mounjaro #weightloss #bodydismorphia."

Former Girls Next Door star Kendra Wilkinson gave one unnamed weight loss injectable a shot. Exactly one, to be precise. “I started the weight loss shots,” she wrote on her Instagram Stories in April 2025. “Only did one. Nevermind. Throwing away!!”

However, she resumed what she called her "GLP-1 journey" in March 2026, writing on Instagram that she was "being really intentional" about her usage this time around.

"For me, it wasn’t just about weight… it was about feeling better, having more energy, and actually trusting the process instead of rushing it," she continued. "I wanted something that felt transparent, supportive, and realistic for my lifestyle."

The Golden Globes host fiercly defended the use of Ozempic in March 2025, calling for people to be more open about using the medication.

“I love it. I’m like, ‘Do it,’” she said on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon. “I have no judgment. If you want to do Ozempic, hell yeah, girl.”

She added, “I want people to feel more comfortable talking about doing it, because I feel like there's this shame,” she continued. “The shame is only from thin people who want you to stay fat. That's really where it's coming from. They're so mad that you're getting thin now, because that's all they have, right? You’re dynamic, you have a good personality, and they're so mad.”

In December 2024, the model said she had once taken Ozempic but stopped after she started competing on Dancing With the Stars the previous fall.

"I took, like, a little bit when it first came out, and everyone was doing it," Nader told Us Weekly. "It made me really nauseous. I liked it—I am not going to lie—and when I went on Dancing with the Stars, I could not do both."

Brooks said she "lost a little bit of the motivation and the strength to work out" by taking the medication. "It was one or the other," she said, "and I picked dancing. I put the shot away."

Dog the Bounty Hunter's daughter shared in November 2024 that she had lost 58 pounds in 10 months thanks to a change in diet and the use of the weight loss medication Tirzepatide, adding, "I am able to look at myself in the mirror and feel so proud of where I've gotten."

But before finding the solution that works for her, she had a rough go with Ozempic. "I hated it," she revealed to E! News. "I could not eat without feeling nauseous. I could not eat at all, sometimes. My body did not like it."

The Real Housewives of New York City star shot down speculation about her glow-up between seasons 14 and 15.

“I think that when you’re in reality TV, it’s so natural to be like, ‘Oh, she got plastic surgery or she did this or she’s on Ozempic,’” she told Us Weekly in October 2024. “I actually f--king hate Ozempic. I would never put needles in myself.”

After several fans speculated on social media that Lizzo used Ozempic to lose weight, following a post she shared in which she showcased a slimmer figure, the Grammy winner posted this video, set to a viral TikTok sound bite of Christoph Waltz's character saying, "It's like a reward" from Django Unchained.

Later, though, the musician admitted she gave some injectibles a shot.

"I tried everything," Lizzo told host Trisha Paytas during a June 2025 episode of the Just Trish podcast, before explaining why she wound up ditching GLP-1 medications early on in her journey. Kate Moss' little sis revealed why getting on Ozempic was "the worst decision I ever made," during a September 2024 episode of her Dream On podcast.

After taking a dosage meant for those roughly 220 pounds or more, the model was struggling to keep any food or water down and landed in the emergency room.

“I literally had a seizure from how dehydrated I was, which honestly was the scariest thing that’s ever happened to me in my life,” she admitted. “My friend had to hold my feet down. It was so scary, the whole situation. My face was clenching up, my whole body was tense.”

The Pioneer Woman star shared on her blog in March 2024 that her 50-pound weight loss in 2022 was not due to taking Ozempic or similar medications.

In August 2023, the 30 Rock alum said on Today With Hoda and Jenna that he lost weight on Ozempic because it supressed his appetite.

In March 2024, his health journey appeared to take a surprising turn. "I've learned to out-eat Ozempic," he said on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon. "I gained 40 pounds."

Later that month, he clarified to E! News that he was joking, adding, "Ozempic did great by me and I was glad to use it."

The Real Housewives of Dubai star opened up about using Ozempic after going through a "midlife crisis" at 45.

"After 40, we all know it's very, very hard to lose weight," she said in the May 22 episode of her podcast Uncut & Uncensored With Caroline Stanbury. "But I met so many 40-year-old women going, 'How have you done it?' And I don't want to lie to you, I used Ozempic, which I think is one of the best tools if you're able to use it."

The Real Housewives of New Jersey star declared "I am not on Ozempic" during a July 2024 Watch What Happens Live interview before hilariously adding, "I'm on Mounjaro, okay. I'm sorry! I love being this weight, I love it! I have so much energy if you couldn't tell."

The Real Housewives of Atlanta alum revealed her failed attempt to lose weight with the injectable medication.

"I tried Ozempic and it didn't work for me," she shared in an April 2024 episode of her misSPELLING podcast, "so I went on Mounjaro, which did do the trick and I did lose weight."

"I think it's very important we understand certain medications are made for certain people," the actress told E! News' Francesca Amiker, "and to not take that away just for glamazon purposes."

#880. O'Shea proud of how team-mates handled Israel games

Dara O'Shea stepped in as Republic of Ireland captain for the last international window in place of the injured Nathan Collins

Republic of Ireland defender Dara O'Shea said he is "proud" of how he and his team-mates came through a trying October international window.

During a four-game Nations League schedule, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side lost away to Kosovo and drew at home to Austria - who they are preparing to face in return fixtures - but it was two games against Israel which tested their resolve.

O'Shea stepped in as captain in the absence of injured skipper Nathan Collins and the 27-year-old acknowledged it "was a tough situation to be in" as they faced Israel in two games on neutral territory.

The first of those resulted in a 3-0 victory for the Irish in Hungary, a game that looked in doubt the previous day when training was delayed as players took a vote on whether to play - amid protests over the Israel-Gaza war - with goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu making himself unavailable for selection.

The sides drew 1-1 in the second meeting in Serbia and, while the saga proved a challenge for all within the Republic of Ireland squad, O'Shea - who missed the second game for personal reasons - paid tribute to his team-mates for the support he received as stand-in skipper.

"I think I was quite lucky, I am really proud to be part of the group, with some great people in it," said the Ipswich Town captain.

"Even the players playing now as well, they are great leaders themselves. I never felt I was fully alone in having to do anything

"There were always people around me. I always keep level-headed, I don't get too high with the highs or too low with the lows."

He added: "Of course it was a difficult time, it was a time that I had to learn stuff about myself, how I was going to react to things. But I think as a group we did excellently.

"It was a tough situation to be in, but we overcame it as best we could. And I am really proud of the group and the staff."

Seamus Coleman has been without a club since leaving Everton at the end of last season

Collins is back to lead the team for Saturday's trip to face Austria in Linz and the final League B3 game at home to Kosovo on Tuesday (both 19:45 GMT).

Also part of the squad is Seamus Coleman, who has taken on a 'hybrid role' despite not being named in manager Hallgrimsson's official 24-man squad.

"It's great to have them [Collins and Coleman] back," O'Shea continued.

"It would have been great if they were there in the last camp as well, but we had some really good people in that last camp who were doing great things.

"Nathan's the captain, so it's always great to have him back in. Seamus' knowledge is so, so valuable to us. I think we are a stronger group when we have them two with us."

Coleman has been without a club since leaving Everton at the end of last season, following 17 years with the Toffees.

The 38-year-old defender recently said he is considering retirement but Republic of Ireland assistant coach John O'Shea is delighted to have the Donegal man around the squad.

"It's us helping Seamus and Seamus helping us," O'Shea said of Coleman's role on the training pitch.

"To see the impact he's having, the quality that remains in his ability and the driving and pushing he's doing for everyone in the group has been good to see. Not much has changed."

#877. Archive, 1990: Peter Shilton wins 125th and final cap of record-breaking England career

9 July 1990: The goalkeeper’s 20-year international career ends at the Italia 90 World Cup

Harry Kane is expected to break the record for England men’s appearances tonight against Croatia at Wembley in the Nations League, overtaking goalkeeper Peter Shilton’s 125 appearances, a record set nearly four decades ago at the World Cup in Italy.

Shilton wore the captain’s armband in his final England appearance in the unloved third-place play-off against Italy in Bari. The Three Lions had previously lost on penalties to West Germany in the semi-finals.

The Guardian’s Ian Ridley, pitch side, reported that Shilton, who announced his retirement from international football that night, said: “I would just like to say how much I have thoroughly enjoyed the last 20 years.”

That joy must have been tempered slightly, though, when, in the 71st minute, Shilton, who had made his international debut against East Germany in 1970, untypically lost concentration, allowing Roberto Baggio to steal the ball as he casually cleared a back pass and scored Italy’s opening goal.

Despite a pinpoint headed equaliser by David Platt, England went down 2-1, with Schillaci scoring a penalty to win the tournament’s Golden Boot. It was also England manager Bobby Robson’s last game in charge. On his rare error, Shilton said of his teammates: “No one, though, seemed to mind much.”

It was goodnight from him and it was goodnight from him. Bobby Robson ended his eight years as keeper of the England keys and Peter Shilton his career as keeper of the England goal, after 125 appearances, in footballing debit but moral credit.

At times, too, it must have seemed like a custodial sentence for Robson, but not on a windy, moonlit Saturday night by the Adriatic at the San Nicola stadium. The loss to Italy was honourable, like the man and certainly in this tournament the team.

The draping banners for Italy saying “Thanks anyway” applied equally to England. “Bravissimo” was the verdict on them of Azeglio Vicini, the host nation’s manager. Robson exuded bonhomie, except that he could not resist a bit of manager-speak about the two goals “which I’m not very happy about”.

Unfortunately for Shilton, 30 minutes before announcing his retirement “I would just like to say how much I have thoroughly enjoyed the last 20 years” his error gave Italy their first goal. No one, though, seemed to mind much.

Robson “made” Shilton play because he wanted him to finish at the top, even though the venerable one was ready to stand aside for Woods. For Robson “I shall miss it greatly. It has been my life for eight years” it was “nice” that the two should end at the same time. ‘No doubt we’ll both be missed,” he added with a smile.

Shilton saved excellently from Ferrara in the first half, tipping his shot on to a post, but after 70 minutes found himself Gary Crosbyed by Baggio as he tried to dribble the ball. Baggio was offside when Schillaci fed him the ball to cut inside Parker and score, but then again Shilton had brought him down as punishment for robbing him. It all evened out.

So did the game 10 minutes later, England’s favourite time. The next manager might even consider beginning his team talk: ‘Right lads. Just imagine we’re one down and there’s 10 minutes to go ...’

Dorigo, who had an excellent first start proving again that as a left-back he is an outstanding left-winger crossed and Platt beat Baresi and his ball-watching defence to thump home a header.

No one could contemplate extra-time, least of all the referee Joel Quiniou, it seemed. Having apparently decided earlier that these teams had had enough of penalties hence his decision to ignore Ancelotti’s handling of Beardsley’s free-kick he changed his mind with five minutes left.

Schillaci fell over Walker’s legs and the ‘little hero’, as Robson called him, stepped up to move out on his own as the top scorer of the tournament with his sixth goal. Italy were denied a third in injury-time when a badly erring linesman flagged Berti offside after he had beautifully headed home Baggio’s cross.

England played their part in an entertaining game. It was less tame than might have been expected and was certainly taken seriously by both sides.

The record will show that Robson’s teams played 95, won 47, drew 29 and lost 19 and that Shilton was one of three Bryan Robson and Butcher the others who spanned his tenure. Indeed, it was the passing of an era, but one that should not be allowed to end.

ITALY: Zenga; Baresi, Bergomi, De Agostini (Berti, 65min), Ferrara, Maldini, Vierchowod, Ancelotti, Giannini (Ferri, 89), Baggio, Schillaci.

ENGLAND: Shilton; Stevens, Walker, Wright (Waddle, 73), Parker, Dorigo, Steven, McMahon (Webb, 73), Platt, Lineker, Beardsley.

#875. Assessing the reasons for Man City's decline in form under Maresca

Enzo Fernandez and Elliot Anderson both cost Manchester City more than Â£100m in the summer

The ongoing international break will give Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca much-needed time to fix the growing issues in his squad.

The Italian made a dream start after taking over from Pep Guardiola in the summer, leading the club to a record seven consecutive victories at the beginning of the Premier League season.

But three consecutive defeats have followed as they have fallen six points adrift of league leaders Arsenal, who are looking in imperious form as they aim to retain their title.

In September, it was announced that City had been found guilty of breaking the Premier League's financial rules, and matches have continued as the club await the outcome of their appeal.

With possible sanctions hanging over them, is City's recent league form down to psychological issues or are there tactical problems Maresca needs to address?

Maresca's dream start turns into nightmare as title hopes hit

Property, football and politics: The links between Manchester and Abu Dhabi explained

Renowned sports psychologist Dr Paul McCarthy has 25 years' experience working in the industry with top clubs in England, Scotland, Germany and France.

McCarthy works on the personal and professional lives of players and says both contribute to how well they perform on the pitch, with the need to "piece together a jigsaw" when situations become disrupted.

"Players are like everyone else - they talk about what is going on in their own lives and things that are topical, especially about uncertain events," McCarthy tells BBC Sport.

"It generates communication with a lot of stories and rumour and over time if there are enough losses, there often becomes a reduced collective efficacy.

"A collective efficacy is a squad's belief in their ability to do what they need to do [to win] and because of their success in the past, that is often shaken a little by consecutive losses."

Man City fan addresses club's midfield problem

City were sitting pretty at the top of the table after a flawless start, but have dropped to third - behind Arsenal and Brighton.

After the guilty verdict was announced during the last international break, Maresca's men won their first game back - against 10-man Liverpool at Anfield - then narrowly overcame Ipswich at Etihad Stadium in their following match.

But they have since lost to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest, with defensive issues exposed and individual mistakes proving costly.

In their first seven games of the season, City did not concede any goals because of individual errors - but that has shifted dramatically in the past three matches, with four mistakes from players contributing to goals.

City have conceded 13 goals after 10 league games - their highest total at this stage of a season since 2008-09, when they had let in 16 - and that has prompted questions about their defensive solidity.

Asked if the uncertainty over the ongoing appeal process may affect the focus and attention of players, McCarthy said: "Yeah, that would be a very reasonable human response.

"When people are uncertain about their future, that uncertainty leads to a lack of perceived control, so uncertainty is often more stressful than bad news and the research shows that.

"So while you are waiting and you don't know the outcome, you are uncertain of where you are and there is that lack of control for a lot of people - they come to training, they play their games and it's outside of their responsibility."

Are Manchester City's players being affected by the charges verdict?

While at Chelsea, in a video for NBC Sports, Maresca discussed his tactics - moving counters into a 3-2-2-3 shape before pushing one up to create the 3-1-6 shape.

He explained using six attackers was a tactic he had employed against Inter Milan to outnumber their back five.

This season, he has adopted the 3-1-6 shape more permanently - trading a second holding midfielder for an extra attacking midfielder.

Coaching a team full of quality footballers, there is logic to wanting to play in a more front-footed and imposing manner, but how well tactics are performed depend on the skillset of the players asked to do them.

City's shape in possession this season has often looked like a 3-1-5-1 or 3-1-6 shape, with Anderson typically the holding midfielder

The big questions come in the form of Elliot Anderson and his midfield partners.

Anderson - naturally more of a roaming midfielder - leans on his physical strengths. At Nottingham Forest, he defended intensely, pressed high and wide, and contributed to attacks. This season, Maresca and his staff have looked to mould him into more of a sitting midfielder after the departure of Rodri in the summer.

Learning that role will take time, as it did for Rodri when he first joined.

It is not problematic in its own right to try to coach a player into a key role, but City have looked exposed through the middle of the pitch more often in recent games.

Anderson, who has largely impressed, has played to his habit - stepping out of a holding midfield position to attempt to press or track opposition players, often looking to win the ball back. Clever opponents have used this to drag him out of position before finding players through the middle.

Enzo Le Fee recognises Anderson's willingness to track him and pulls wide

With Anderson vacating the central area, Brian Brobbey is able to drop in and receive the ball directly from his centre-back

With City looking to press high and often in a man-to-man fashion, Anderson has had to cover more space with his partners in midfield lacking the physicality required to support him.

When City are in possession, Enzo Fernandez - often one of City's midfield three - makes frequent attacking runs off the ball into the final third. When this happens, City can find themselves with as few as two or three players behind the ball, giving opponents favourable conditions to counter-attack if they can break the initial press.

Here, City lose the ball. Anderson is drawn out wide whilst Fernandez on the far side remains high and above the line of the ball, leaving City exposed in the middle

For Maresca, the issue is less around the shape, and more around losing the ball in the first instance. After the loss to Forest, he said: "You concede transitions when you lose the ball, and when you don't win duels."

Further concerns arise when assessing the skillset of the players behind Anderson.

Gianluigi Donnarumma is not a goalkeeper renowned for his ball-playing ability. The defensive cohort are serviceable on the ball but have made costly errors under pressure, playing out from the back, this season too.

City have four players near or behind the ball before Josko Gvardiol is dispossessed. Nottingham Forest, with four attackers of their own, score from this turnover

Guardiola's solution to mitigate some of these issues last season came in the form of asking midfielders to shoulder more ball-playing responsibility.

The loss of Rodri and especially Bernardo Silva, who would drop deep and take City from their own goal into midfield alone, have made City's problems more obvious.

As good as Anderson is, he is not a player who can single-handedly resolve build-up play as Bernardo Silva did, but Ayyoub Bouaddi may be somebody that could be used in this manner as we saw him against Brazil's press in the World Cup.
